title: Prove real multi-country national regional and local retrieval
method: Eight cited passages were copied from official HTTPS responses after HTML or XML tags were removed and whitespace was collapsed. Each passage is a substring of that response. The index is those passages, not a full code and not a pinned dataset payload. Latin queries are ranked by searchCompactPostings with the pinned FTS5 unicode61 tokenizer. Arabic uses tokenize strategy arabic and Japanese uses tokenize strategy cjk-unigram, with the same BM25 weights and the same contribution function. That function matched searchCompactPostings on every Latin judgment and on the shared-token probes to an absolute tolerance of 1e-9. Jurisdiction exclusion drops a hit whose jurisdiction_id is in excluded_jurisdiction_ids and then keeps k hits. isolateStrictFilters and hitMatchesStrictFilters apply the labelled jurisdiction as a placeIds allow-list. The two filters kept the same ids on every judgment and probe. Recall is measured only on the filtered list. A pinned FTS5 recall is also recorded. Empty pinned query terms are not treated as cross-language recall.

bm25.length: title token count times 5 plus body token count times 1

known_limitations: No judgment decides that an instrument binds a person, act, or dispute. legal_conclusion and applicability stay not_claimed.
The index contains eight cited passages. It is not the full statute, not every article on the fetched page, and not the pinned Hugging Face dataset bytes.
Recall is labelled-passage recall at 5 after jurisdiction exclusion. It is not a worldwide corpus recall and it is not cross-language recall.
The Dutch article URL redirected to the whole-code HTML. Artikel 1 was copied from that response.
The German consolidation page is headed Nichtamtliches Inhaltsverzeichnis. It is not the Bundesgesetzblatt promulgation copy.
The Bavarian article page did not contain the word amtlich. It cites the 15 December 1998 Bekanntmachung. That citation is not treated as a check of the GVBl copy.
The Noord-Holland passage keeps the retrieved spacing in "ontwikkeling ,".

The Amsterdam labelled passage is Gemeenteblad 2026, 107760, Artikel I, including the page spelling "voortuigen". The page also says the verordening enters into force on 1 May 2026. That sentence is not applied to anyone.

CVDR72510, the consolidated Amsterdam APV labelled Geldend van 14-10-2026 t/m heden, was fetched and was not the indexed passage. The token verordening is absent from the indexed article, so the verordening probe does not return it.
Provinciaal blad 2026, 2410 was fetched as a later amendment witness and was not the indexed regional passage.
Arabic retrieval uses the production arabic tokenizer. The pinned FTS5 reader returns no query terms and pinned recall 0. That zero is not relabelled as same-script recall.

Japanese retrieval uses cjk-unigram. Hiragana and kana are not tokens. The Han characters in the query occur in the cited article. The pinned FTS5 reader again returns no query terms and pinned recall 0. There is no dictionary segmentation and no cross-language match.
The Egypt PDF text was not transcribed. Its body is the same SHA-256 recorded for WWL-025. Municipal coverage stays unsupported because the snapshot has no Egypt municipal row.
Response SHA-256 values identify the retrieved HTTP bodies, including page chrome, and are not publisher revisions. No redistribution license was read from these pages.
The audit command checks the fixture contract. It does not fetch these URLs again and it does not re-score the index.
